To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured 3d diffuse scattering from protein crystal structures, that we have shown that the data can be modeled with a simple liquid-like motion model and with normal mode models, and that the latter can be refined against both Bragg and diffus scattering.

3D diffuse scattering data can be collected from protein crystals using standard data collection techniques, and that a coarse-grained normal mode model provides the best description of both Bragg and the diffuse scattering from the cyclophilin crystals.

1) we measured and modeled diffuse X-ray scattering from protein crystals using standard crystallo-graphic techniques, 2) our results are consistent with the proteins undergoing liquid-like motions, and 3) we have shown that modeling protein motions can be an integrated part of routine crystallography.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of methods to collect and analyze X-ray diffuse scattering from macromolecular crystals, and to apply the results to structural models.
the measurement and analysis of diffuse scattering from macromolecular crystals, with the goal of understanding and modeling the underlying dynamics.
the measurement of diffuse scattering in protein crystals and with the development and testing of a model of protein motions that is compatible with the data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diffuse scattering can provide useful structural information about protein dynamics.

diffuse scattering can be used as a tool to validate structural models that incorporate protein motions, but that the data are not currently of sufficient quality to be used to derive protein motions.
diffuse scattering is a useful addition to the arsenal of techniques available to study the dynamics of proteins in the solid state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the diffuse data are consistent with the protein motion resembling diffusion in a fluid or vibrations of a hard solid.
the combination of the LLM and the NM models is the most promising approach for the modeling of diffuse scattering from proteins.
the LLM and NL models are both consistent with the data and can be used to describe the protein dynamics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diffuse scattering can provide information that can help to constrain protein dynamics, and this can be achieved with minimal additional effort in the data collection process.
diffuse X-ray scattering is a rich source of structural dynamics information that can be used to complement Bragg scattering.
diffuse scattering can be measured from protein crystals with the same X-ray data collection methods that are used to collect the Bragg scattering, and the resulting data are amenable to modeling.
